summary: The transportation matrix is nonnegative and column-stochastic, has the required row sums, gives the prescribed centroid, and has determinant equal to the stated product; the induced affine-volume argument and all degenerate cases are correct. The simplex-centroid depth bound then yields the normalized depth inequality. In the six-cone application, the barycentric slacks, fiber scale, threshold simplification, convexity of the depth superlevel set, polygon area, strict rational comparison, and final constant comparison all check exactly.
